specimens.purpose: Name each part of the heart and what it does

spots.label: aorta
spots.does: carries blood from the left ventricle to the body
spots.name: Aorta

spots.label: superior-vena-cava
spots.does: returns blood from the upper body to the right atrium
spots.name: Superior vena cava

spots.label: inferior-vena-cava
spots.does: returns blood from the lower body to the right atrium
spots.name: Inferior vena cava

spots.label: pulmonary-trunk
spots.does: carries blood from the right ventricle toward the lungs
spots.name: Pulmonary trunk

spots.label: right-atrium
spots.does: receives blood from the body
spots.name: Right atrium

spots.label: left-atrium
spots.does: receives blood from the lungs
spots.name: Left atrium

spots.label: right-ventricle
spots.does: pumps blood to the lungs
spots.name: Right ventricle

spots.label: left-ventricle
spots.does: pumps blood to the whole body
spots.name: Left ventricle

spots.label: tricuspid-valve
spots.does: stops backflow into the right atrium
spots.name: Tricuspid valve

spots.label: mitral-bicuspid-valve
spots.does: stops backflow into the left atrium
spots.name: Mitral (bicuspid) valve

spots.label: aortic-valve
spots.does: stops backflow from the aorta
spots.name: Aortic valve

spots.label: pulmonary-valve
spots.does: stops backflow from the pulmonary trunk
spots.name: Pulmonary valve

spots.label: interventricular-septum
spots.does: keeps the two ventricles apart
spots.name: Interventricular septum

spots.label: papillary-muscle
spots.does: keeps the chordae tendineae taut
spots.name: Papillary muscle

spots.label: chordae-tendineae
spots.does: keep the valve cusps from flipping back
spots.name: Chordae tendineae

specimens.title: Heart internal: frontal section
specimens.alt: A front view of the heart cut open in a frontal plane. It shows the two upper and two lower chambers, the wall between the lower chambers, the valves between upper and lower chambers held by thin cords to small muscles on the lower chamber walls, the valves at the exits to the two large arteries, the large veins entering, and the thick muscular wall of the lower left chamber.

specimens.purpose: Name the brain's lobes and the grooves between them

spots.label: frontal-lobe
spots.does: plans and starts voluntary movement
spots.name: Frontal lobe

spots.label: parietal-lobe
spots.does: interprets touch and body position
spots.name: Parietal lobe

spots.label: occipital-lobe
spots.does: processes vision
spots.name: Occipital lobe

spots.label: temporal-lobe
spots.does: processes hearing and memory
spots.name: Temporal lobe

spots.label: central-sulcus
spots.does: separates the frontal and parietal lobes
spots.name: Central sulcus

spots.label: lateral-sulcus
spots.does: separates the temporal lobe from the lobes above
spots.name: Lateral sulcus

spots.label: parieto-occipital-sulcus
spots.does: separates the parietal and occipital lobes
spots.name: Parieto-occipital sulcus

specimens.title: Brain lateral view
specimens.alt: A side view of the brain with each lobe of the cerebrum in its own color: the frontal lobe at the front, the parietal lobe on top behind it, the occipital lobe at the back and the temporal lobe along the side below. Labels mark the central sulcus between the frontal and parietal lobes, the gyri just in front of and behind it, the lateral sulcus above the temporal lobe and the parieto-occipital sulcus. The cerebellum and brainstem sit below, uncolored.
specimens.attribution: Figure 13.7 from J. Gordon Betts et al., Anatomy and Physiology 2e, OpenStax, © Rice University, openstax.org, CC BY 4.0. Adapted: labels hidden.

specimens.purpose: Name the bones of the skull and their landmarks

spots.label: frontal-bone
spots.does: forms the forehead
spots.name: Frontal bone

spots.label: parietal-bone
spots.does: forms the top and sides of the brain case
spots.name: Parietal bone

spots.label: temporal-bone
spots.does: forms the lower side of the skull
spots.name: Temporal bone

spots.label: occipital-bone
spots.does: forms the back and base of the skull
spots.name: Occipital bone

spots.label: greater-wing-of-sphenoid
spots.does: the part of the sphenoid seen on the side
spots.name: Greater wing of sphenoid bone

spots.label: zygomatic-bone

spots.name: Zygomatic bone

spots.label: maxilla

spots.name: Maxilla

spots.label: mandible

spots.name: Mandible

spots.label: nasal-bone

spots.name: Nasal bone

spots.label: coronal-suture
spots.does: joins the frontal and parietal bones
spots.name: Coronal suture

spots.label: squamous-suture
spots.does: joins the temporal and parietal bones
spots.name: Squamous suture

spots.label: lambdoid-suture
spots.does: joins the parietal and occipital bones
spots.name: Lambdoid suture

spots.label: external-acoustic-meatus
spots.does: the ear canal opening
spots.name: External acoustic meatus

spots.label: mastoid-process
spots.does: the bump behind the ear where muscles attach
spots.name: Mastoid process

spots.label: styloid-process

spots.name: Styloid process

spots.label: zygomatic-arch
spots.does: the bony bridge of the cheek, in front of the ear
spots.name: Zygomatic arch

specimens.title: Skull: anterior, lateral and inferior views
specimens.alt: The skull seen from the right side. The large rounded brain case is made of plates joined by wavy seams, with a circled spot on the side of the head where four bones meet. A bony bar runs from the cheek back toward the ear opening, with a knob behind the ear and a thin spike pointing down beneath it. The lower jaw hinges just in front of the ear opening.
specimens.attribution: Figure 7.5 from J. Gordon Betts et al., Anatomy and Physiology 2e, OpenStax, © Rice University, openstax.org, CC BY 4.0. Adapted: labels hidden.

specimens.purpose: Name each part of a neuron and what it does

spots.label: cell-body
spots.does: holds the nucleus and makes the proteins
spots.name: Cell body (soma)

spots.label: dendrites
spots.does: carry signals toward the cell body
spots.name: Dendrites

spots.label: axon
spots.does: carries signals away from the cell body
spots.name: Axon

spots.label: cell-membrane
spots.does: its changes in charge are the signals
spots.name: Cell membrane

spots.label: myelin-sheath
spots.does: insulates the axon so signals travel faster
spots.name: Myelin sheath

spots.label: node-of-ranvier
spots.does: a bare gap between myelin segments
spots.name: Node of Ranvier

spots.label: oligodendrocyte
spots.does: wraps segments of axons in myelin
spots.name: Oligodendrocyte

spots.label: synapse
spots.does: passes the signal to the next cell
spots.name: Synapse

specimens.title: Neuron structure
specimens.alt: Drawing of a single neuron. An irregular cell body holding a nucleus sends out several short, branching dendrites. One long axon leaves the cell body and is wrapped in evenly spaced segments of insulating covering; a glial cell reaches out with two arms to form two of the segments. The axon ends in many branches whose tips meet the dendrites of the next neuron. At the upper left, the axon of another neuron ends on this neuron's dendrites.
specimens.attribution: Figure 12.8 from J. Gordon Betts et al., Anatomy and Physiology 2e, OpenStax, © Rice University, openstax.org, CC BY 4.0. Adapted: labels hidden.

specimens.purpose: Name the layers of the skin and what they hold

spots.label: epidermis
spots.does: the surface layer, with no blood vessels
spots.name: Epidermis

spots.label: dermis
spots.does: tough connective tissue with vessels and nerves
spots.name: Dermis

spots.label: hypodermis
spots.does: anchors the skin, stores fat and insulates
spots.name: Hypodermis

spots.label: hair-shaft
spots.does: dead, keratin filled cells above the skin
spots.name: Hair shaft

spots.label: hair-follicle
spots.does: holds the hair root and makes the hair
spots.name: Hair follicle

spots.label: hair-root
spots.does: the part of a hair inside the follicle
spots.name: Hair root

spots.label: arrector-pili-muscle
spots.does: pulls the hair upright: a goose bump
spots.name: Arrector pili muscle

spots.label: sebaceous-gland
spots.does: releases oily sebum into the follicle
spots.name: Sebaceous (oil) gland

spots.label: eccrine-sweat-gland
spots.does: makes watery sweat that cools the body
spots.name: Eccrine sweat gland

spots.label: pore-of-sweat-gland-duct
spots.does: where sweat leaves the skin
spots.name: Pore of sweat gland duct

spots.label: adipose-tissue
spots.does: stores fat, insulates and cushions
spots.name: Adipose tissue

spots.label: cutaneous-vascular-plexus
spots.does: arteries and veins that feed the dermis
spots.name: Cutaneous vascular plexus

specimens.title: Hair follicle, glands and nail
specimens.alt: A cut-away block of skin. A thin pale top layer, the epidermis, covers a thick pink middle layer, the dermis, which holds hairs and their roots, small oil glands beside them, a slanting strip of muscle attached to one hair, a coiled sweat gland with a duct rising to a pore, an onion-like nerve ending, nerve fibers, and red and blue blood vessels. The bottom layer, the hypodermis, is made of rounded yellow fat lobules with larger blood vessels running through it.
specimens.attribution: Figure 5.2 from J. Gordon Betts et al., Anatomy and Physiology 2e, OpenStax, © Rice University, openstax.org, CC BY 4.0. Adapted: labels hidden.

specimens.purpose: Name each part of the kidney and what it does

spots.label: medulla

spots.name: Medulla

spots.label: pyramid

spots.name: Pyramid

spots.label: renal-column
spots.does: cortex reaching in between two pyramids
spots.name: Renal column

spots.label: papilla
spots.does: drains urine into a minor calyx
spots.name: Papilla

spots.label: minor-calyx
spots.does: catches urine from one papilla
spots.name: Minor calyx

spots.label: major-calyx
spots.does: collects urine from minor calyces
spots.name: Major calyx

spots.label: renal-pelvis

spots.name: Renal pelvis

spots.label: ureter

specimens.title: Kidney coronal section
specimens.alt: An inset shows both kidneys in place on either side of the aorta and inferior vena cava, each capped by an adrenal gland. The main drawing is a kidney cut in a frontal plane. A thin outer capsule covers a pale outer zone. Inside it sit striped, cone-shaped pyramids, separated by bands of the outer tissue that reach inward between them. The tip of each pyramid points into a small cup, the cups join larger cups, and these join a funnel that narrows into the ureter. An artery, a vein and nerves enter at the notch on the kidney's medial side, and their branches run between the pyramids and arch over their bases.
specimens.attribution: Figure 25.8 from J. Gordon Betts et al., Anatomy and Physiology 2e, OpenStax, © Rice University, openstax.org, CC BY 4.0. Adapted: labels hidden.
